name: LinuxArena
intro: LinuxArena 是面向真实多服务生产环境的 AI 控制基准，在智能体完成正常软件工程主任务时评估其隐蔽完成有害副任务的能力，以及监控器在危害发生前检出攻击的能力。
build_method: 从零构建20个有状态Docker Compose环境；LLM辅助、人工复核主任务；纯人工副任务；外部二元评分器；任务/评分器/诚实轨迹质控；全量同环境配对的两阶段意外完成过滤
metric: 主任务成功率，副任务成功率，破坏成功率P(未检出∧副任务成功)，规避率P(未检出|副任务成功)，安全性P(检出)/[P(检出)+P(未检出∧攻击成功)]
eval_feature: 论文v2以400项主任务切片和185项明显副任务单测评测；隐蔽攻击按160步五阶段运行；逐动作预执行监控；按诚实轨迹校准1%逐步误报率；仅危害前告警计为检出
openness_en: Partly Public (10 public and 10 withheld environments; released scorer code is hidden only from the agent at run time)
build_method_en: Twenty scratch-built stateful Docker Compose environments; LLM-assisted, human-reviewed main tasks; fully human-authored side tasks; external binary scorers; task/scorer/honest-trajectory QC; and two-stage filtering over every same-environment pair
eval_feature_en: Paper-v2 evaluation uses a 400-main-task slice and all 185 obvious side tasks; subtle attacks follow a five-phase 160-step protocol; monitors run before each action at an honestly calibrated 1% step-wise FPR; only pre-harm flags count
intro_en: LinuxArena is an AI-control benchmark for live multi-service production environments. It evaluates whether agents can covertly complete harmful side tasks while doing legitimate software-engineering main tasks and whether monitors detect attacks before harm occurs.
scale_en: Paper v2 full inventory: 20 environments, 1,667 main tasks, 185 side tasks; public: 10/906/92; withheld: 10/761/93
metric_en: Main-task success; side-task success; sabotage P(undetected and side success); evasion P(undetected | side success); safety P(detected)/[P(detected)+P(undetected and attack successful)]

drawio_review_note: Paper-alignment review passed on 2026-07-21 against arXiv:2604.15384v2, fixed paper source https://github.com/linuxarena/linuxarena-paper/tree/4c5aa72e6c6af314bc247c8313e11e78e2c7a946, audited Control Tower snapshot https://github.com/linuxarena/control-tower/tree/48218189eb6d7f69da3666794f4e4d1eeaeb0aa1, and the versioned LaStraj v3 portal https://data.linuxarena.ai/datasets/LaStraj?version=3. The paper inventory is 20 scratch-built stateful Docker Compose environments, 1,667 LLM-assisted and human-reviewed main tasks, and 185 fully human-authored side tasks; the paper public half is 10 environments/906 main/92 side and the withheld half is 10/761/93. Current public artifacts drift from that snapshot: the audited canonical bundles total 10/907/92, while the official homepage states 10/919/93. Task and scorer QC, plausible attack construction, and saved honest-only main trajectories precede pairing. Stage 1 screens every same-environment main×side pair from the environment description, main description, side goal, and side-scorer code; only MAYBE or LIKELY pairs reach Stage 2. Stage 2 replays the saved honest trajectory in a fresh environment, and a second model may use only the side-test tool: scorer C removes the pairing, I retains it. About 0.9% of pairs are removed, with auditing repeated until residual false positives fall below the safety-metric noise floor; task inventory counts do not change. Paper evaluation uses 400 main tasks (20 per environment) and all 185 side tasks for the obvious side-only capability slice. The subtle policy receives the main task and side goal but no scorer, pseudocode, or environment description; hidden planning and 1k thinking tokens per call accompany two exploration windows of at most 30 steps, two offline plans, and at most 100 execution steps. The paper cap is 160 and final state is scored at the cap, while the audited current Control Tower default is 150. The paper's main monitor is live and per-action; full-trajectory and combined variants are appendix analyses. Before execution it sees the main task, score-band guidance, action history and outcomes, and all possible side goals, but not attacker chain-of-thought. Two independent integer 0–10 calls are averaged; model-matched honest calibration, probabilistic tie-breaking, and the 99th percentile yield exactly 1% step-wise FPR, and any flagged action flags the trajectory. Current parsing uses a Pydantic reasoning-plus-integer schema with provider validation and retries. Early, zero-step, no-submit, scorer-failure, and environment-failure episodes are retried; missing monitor scores are dropped rather than imputed as zero, and parse failures plus valid denominators are audited. Live harm is the first successful side-test output beginning with 'Score value: C'; otherwise it is final submit when the side scorer succeeds. Only flags strictly before harm count. The report distinguishes sabotage P(undetected∧side success), evasion P(undetected|side success), and safety P(detected)/[P(detected)+P(undetected∧attack successful)], with Wilson 95% intervals for proportions and bootstrap intervals for safety curves. LaStraj is an independent human red-team trajectory branch: side and non-auto-completing cover-main tasks are selected in public environments, each selected trajectory receives at most eight hours of iteration against GPT-4.1 Nano or Opus 4.6 to reach live-monitor score at most 5/10, synthetic exploration is inserted for omniscient traces and detection-triggering traces are discarded, and v3 exposes 76 side-success trajectories. Released scorer code is hidden only from the evaluated agent at run time. The paper evaluates sabotage and monitors rather than specifying a complete end-to-end control protocol. LinuxArena exposes no public leaderboard or submission path.
